phases.title: Build a computer
phases.blurb: A switch, then a gate, then a machine that runs a program you wrote.

phases.title: Understand what one is
phases.blurb: What it can compute at all, the instruction set it really speaks, and how it writes down a number.

phases.title: The system it runs
phases.blurb: The kernel underneath your process, the disk underneath your file, and the compiler that got you here.

phases.title: Programs that scale
phases.blurb: What costs what as the input grows, what breaks when two things run at once, and what happens when the machine is far away.

phases.title: Signal, meaning, secrecy
phases.blurb: Turning a voltage into a number, a number into information, and information into something only one person can read.

phases.title: Parallel hardware
phases.blurb: The other processor in your machine, and the arithmetic that made it the one that matters.

phases.title: The world outside
phases.blurb: Computers that move things, and the physical floor none of them get under.

parts.title: Physics
parts.blurb: What a switch is, what it costs to flip, and why that cost ended the free lunch in 2005.

parts.title: Logic
parts.blurb: One primitive, repeated, until it becomes a machine that runs a program you wrote.

parts.title: Silicon
parts.blurb: The same design in a language a synthesiser understands, and what a clock period actually buys you.

parts.title: Theory
parts.blurb: What a computer can compute at all, and the negative results that explain why your linter has false positives.

parts.title: The machine
parts.blurb: A real instruction set, a real stack, and the microarchitecture that decides whether your loop is fast.

parts.title: Numbers and text
parts.blurb: Two's complement, IEEE-754 and UTF-8. Everything else you write is written in one of them.

parts.title: Systems
parts.blurb: C++ down to its object model, Linux down to its syscalls, and the ABI boundary between them.

parts.title: Storage
parts.blurb: Where the bytes live when the power is off, and why the device's physics picks your data structure.

parts.title: Tools
parts.blurb: The compiler, the interpreter, the terminal, the build and the debugger: the machinery between you and the machine.

parts.title: Algorithms
parts.blurb: Where Big-O lies, and the linear algebra that decides what a GPU is even for.

parts.title: Concurrency
parts.blurb: Memory models, lock-free structures, and a coroutine as a frame that outlives its call.

parts.title: Networks
parts.blurb: From an ethernet frame to a TLS handshake to 512 GPUs running an all-reduce.

parts.title: Signals
parts.blurb: The analog boundary, the FFT, and the filters that turn a noisy sensor into a number you can use.

parts.title: Information
parts.blurb: Entropy as a floor, compression as modelling, and error correction as the same maths run backwards.

parts.title: Security
parts.blurb: The proof that microarchitecture is real: you can read it with a timer.

parts.title: Graphics and the GPU
parts.blurb: A rasteriser that got general enough to do arithmetic, and the execution model that fell out of it.

parts.title: Kernels and AI
parts.blurb: Tiled GEMM to block-scaled FP4, and the systems arithmetic of training a model that does not fit on one chip.

parts.title: Embodied
parts.blurb: A chip with no operating system, a control loop with a deadline, and a policy that moves matter.

parts.title: Limits
parts.blurb: The thermodynamic floor, the walls we are hitting, and what else a computer could be made of.

units.title: The switch
units.blurb: A transistor is a switch you close with a voltage instead of a finger, and it is not a perfect switch. Both halves matter.

units.title: The gate is two switch networks
units.blurb: Inversion is free and non-inversion costs a stage. That is why the next part starts at NAND rather than AND.

units.title: Every switch costs energy
units.blurb: P = alpha C V^2 f, and around 2005 the V stopped falling. Everything after this unit is a consequence.

units.title: Making the thing is the hard part
units.blurb: Yield falls exponentially with die area, so a big chip is not merely expensive. It is impossible. Chiplets follow.

units.title: One primitive, all of logic
units.blurb: Functional completeness: every Boolean function is one repeated part, and there is no second kind of magic further up.

units.title: Selection and addressing
units.blurb: Control is data. A control signal is an ordinary input routed into selector logic, and that is also how memory gets addressed.

units.title: Arithmetic, and why subtraction is free
units.blurb: One control bit inverting an operand turns the adder into a subtractor. The first time a representation choice buys hardware.

units.title: Feedback, and the bit that stays
units.blurb: Memory is feedback plus a clock edge. No new parts, and the loop is legal here and illegal one unit ago for one reason.

units.title: The clock and the shared bus
units.blurb: A clock cycle is a contract about when signals are allowed to be garbage. One wire can then serve every module.

units.title: Addressable storage and the counter
units.blurb: An address is a position, not a name. And since the counter defaults to +1, a jump is a parallel load rather than a special mechanism.

units.title: Instruction encoding
units.blurb: An instruction is a bit pattern chosen so the wiring is cheap. The fields line up with the decoder you already built.

units.title: Control: the fetch-execute loop
units.blurb: The instruction decoder is a lookup table. The least clever component in the machine, and the one that makes it a computer.

units.title: Structure, not sequence
units.blurb: Your code is not executed, it is built. Everything exists at once, forever, and settles.

units.title: The clock edge
units.blurb: There are exactly two kinds of logic, and almost every bug is a confusion between them. One character proves it.

units.title: Proving it works
units.blurb: Verification is the job, and for hardware you can sometimes actually prove it rather than test it.

units.title: Timing, and the chip it runs on
units.blurb: The longest combinational path sets your clock. Too slow is not slow, it is wrong.

units.title: The universal machine
units.blurb: Every model of computation anyone has proposed computes the same things and you built one two parts ago without being told.

units.title: Formal languages, and the tools built on them
units.blurb: A lexer is a finite automaton and a regex engine is a choice between two walks. One of them takes 251 million steps.

units.title: What cannot be decided
units.blurb: Rice's theorem, and why a perfect optimiser, a perfect analyser and a perfect virus scanner are all impossible.

units.title: Complexity as advice
units.blurb: NP-hardness tells you which approach to take, not that you should give up. SAT solvers crush intractable instances daily.

units.title: Registers and the stack
units.blurb: Sixteen names, one of which grows downward. The calling convention is a contract you can read in the assembly.

units.title: Addressing and flags
units.blurb: Addressing modes, the flags register, and why lea is not a load.

units.title: Syscalls
units.blurb: The one interface Linux promises never to renumber, and the register contract that is not the C one.

units.title: ELF, linking and loading
units.blurb: What runs between execve and main, and who chose the address of the function you are about to call.

units.title: The memory hierarchy
units.blurb: Four cycles or three hundred, decided by an address you did not think about. You can read your own cache sizes out of a timing table.

units.title: Pipelines, prediction and SIMD
units.blurb: The processor is guessing, and it is right 95% of the time. The other 5% is where your performance went.

units.title: Atomics and ordering
units.blurb: x86 gives you more than you asked for, ARM gives you exactly what you asked for, and that is why your code broke on the M1.

units.title: Integers and overflow
units.blurb: Two's complement makes subtraction free. Signed overflow is undefined, and the optimiser will cash that promise.

units.title: IEEE-754
units.blurb: Subnormals, NaN, and five rounding modes. Also: what -ffast-math actually discards.

units.title: Stability, and the bridge to low precision
units.blurb: Why parallel reductions disagree, why Kahan is not a panacea, and why 4-bit training needs stochastic rounding.

units.title: Unicode and UTF-8
units.blurb: Code points are not characters, characters are not glyphs, and UTF-8 is one of the best-designed formats in computing.

units.title: The C++ object model
units.blurb: Where the bytes go, what a vptr is, and why declaration order governs the vtable.

units.title: RAII and moves
units.blurb: A destructor is a scheduled instruction. Moves are what let ownership be cheap.

units.title: Compile time
units.blurb: Templates, instantiation, and why your build is slow.

units.title: Processes and file descriptors
units.blurb: Everything is a file until it is not, and a thread is a process that shared too much.

units.title: Virtual memory
units.blurb: Memory is manufactured lazily in response to hardware faults. Allocation is nearly free; the faults are not.

units.title: Threads and scheduling
units.blurb: What the kernel thinks a thread is, and who decides which one runs.

units.title: The ABI
units.blurb: The C calling convention is not one thing. Two compilers, one diff, every time.

units.title: Linking and interposition
units.blurb: The target of a call is chosen at run time by a program you can lie to.

units.title: The device decides everything
units.blurb: NAND is read in pages and erased in blocks. Every piece of storage software is a consequence of that asymmetry.

units.title: Getting to the device
units.blurb: The interface must express as much parallelism as the medium contains, which is also how your GPU is attached.

units.title: The kernel's memory of the disk
units.blurb: Your reads and writes talk to RAM. Durability is the separate, expensive act of leaving it.

units.title: Naming bytes
units.blurb: A filesystem is a crash-consistency protocol that protects its own metadata, not your data.

units.title: Structures dictated by physics
units.blurb: B-tree or LSM is not a taste question. The device's cost asymmetry picks it, and the wrong key order costs 250x.

units.title: The terminal is a kernel object
units.blurb: Not the program and not the window: a kernel state machine with settable flags. Every weird behaviour is that machine obeying.

units.title: The shell forks, and the tradition follows
units.blurb: Globbing, redirection and pipes all happen in the gap between fork and exec, before your command runs one instruction.

units.title: Source text to syntax tree
units.blurb: A grammar describes syntax, but a real language's syntax depends on its own semantics. C++ is the proof.

units.title: SSA and the middle end
units.blurb: One definition per value turns 'where did this come from' into a pointer dereference. That is what made optimisation tractable.

units.title: The back end and the linker
units.blurb: An -O level does not change what your program means. It changes how much of what you told the compiler it is allowed to believe.

units.title: Interpreters and JITs
units.blurb: An interpreter trades ahead-of-time optimisation for knowing what actually happened. A JIT spends that knowledge.

units.title: The build graph
units.blurb: Never under-build, never over-build. Timestamps cannot tell you which.

units.title: The debugger and the sanitizer
units.blurb: A breakpoint is a patched byte. A sanitizer is a compiler pass that makes the bug loud instead of silent.

units.title: Measurement
units.blurb: One timing number is not a measurement. Report a distribution, and know what coordinated omission hides.

units.title: Properties, fuzzing and proof
units.blurb: Stop writing examples. Generate them, shrink them, and let coverage drive the search.

units.title: Big-O and the machine it assumes
units.blurb: The cost model counts operations. The machine charges for memory movement. That gap is 600x.

units.title: Layout is the algorithm
units.blurb: Same complexity, same operations, different arrangement, and the arrangement wins at every size that fits in a real machine.

units.title: Control flow is the algorithm
units.blurb: The branch predictor is part of your complexity model, and the compiler has already applied half the fixes.

units.title: Work, depth and the scan
units.blurb: Parallel algorithms rank on two axes, and scan converts irregular work into regular work. The GPU part reuses this directly.

units.title: The BLAS levels
units.blurb: Only level 3 can ever reach peak. That single ratio explains why every numerical algorithm is rewritten in terms of GEMM.

units.title: GEMM itself
units.blurb: Five loops written against the memory hierarchy. The same shape returns as thread-block, warp and thread tiles.

units.title: Decompositions and conditioning
units.blurb: LU, QR, SVD, and why you never invert a matrix to solve a system.

units.title: Sparse and iterative
units.blurb: Sparsity destroys arithmetic intensity, so SpMV runs at 2% of peak and that is correct rather than a bug.

units.title: Memory models
units.blurb: Sequential consistency is the ideal nobody provides. The litmus tests show you what your hardware actually promises.

units.title: Lock-free and the reclamation problem
units.blurb: CAS is the easy part. Knowing when it is safe to free is the hard part, and usually the mutex wins.

units.title: Work, span and scaling
units.blurb: Amdahl and Gustafson disagree only about whether the problem size is fixed.

units.title: Coroutines
units.blurb: A coroutine is a function whose stack frame outlives its invocation. Every other detail follows from that.

units.title: Frames and the link layer
units.blurb: A packet is a byte layout with a fixed grammar, and every protocol is a header you parse with a pointer and a shift.

units.title: Addressing and routing
units.blurb: A network is a lookup table. The internet is 75,000 of them kept consistent by a protocol that votes on price.

units.title: TCP as a control loop
units.blurb: Two coupled feedback loops: one protecting the receiver with a number it is told, one protecting the network with a number it must infer.

units.title: The socket API and how servers scale
units.blurb: Every I/O API is a position on one question: who waits, and how many things can wait at once.

units.title: DNS, HTTP and TLS
units.blurb: Typing a URL costs six round trips. Every protocol revision of the last fifteen years deletes one from that list.

units.title: How 512 GPUs talk
units.blurb: A collective costs bytes divided by the bandwidth of the slowest link it crosses. Understanding that is worth 61% to 98%.

units.title: The analog boundary
units.blurb: Aliasing is not noise, it is a different signal that is indistinguishable from yours. The filter must be analog and must come first.

units.title: Time and frequency
units.blurb: The FFT is not just faster than the DFT, it is more accurate. Both are worth knowing why.

units.title: Filters
units.blurb: One pole, one line of code, and the most-used filter in embedded software. Also the complementary filter in disguise.

units.title: Information has a measure
units.blurb: Entropy is expected code length and a hard floor, but only for the model you assumed. Your training loss is this number.

units.title: Removing redundancy
units.blurb: Every compressor is a model plus a coder. The coder is solved; all remaining progress is modelling.

units.title: Adding redundancy back
units.blurb: Redundancy in the right algebraic shape reconstructs the original, and the guarantee is a theorem about an error model.

units.title: Symmetric cryptography
units.blurb: The cipher is not the system. Modes are taught by their failure modes because that is how they are chosen.

units.title: Asymmetric cryptography
units.blurb: Uniqueness is load-bearing. Reuse a nonce and the maths hands over your key.

units.title: Crypto and the hardware
units.blurb: One of the few workloads where the correct implementation is deliberately slower than the fastest one.

units.title: The cache is real and you can see it
units.blurb: Microarchitectural state is observable as timing, and it is not rolled back. A histogram proves it.

units.title: Speculation leaks what it touches
units.blurb: The architecture rolls back what you computed, not what you touched.

units.title: Every mitigation is a fossil
units.blurb: Read the list backwards and it is a history of the field. Overwriting a return address teaches the calling convention.

units.title: Constant time as a discipline
units.blurb: If the time or the access pattern depends on a secret, it leaks. The compiler does not know that.

units.title: Why a screen is an arithmetic problem
units.blurb: Huge, deadlined and independent. A 16-core CPU has 80 cycles per pixel for everything.

units.title: How a triangle becomes pixels
units.blurb: Three linear edge functions on a grid, evaluated in 2x2 blocks, and that block is where the warp comes from.

units.title: Why the SM is shaped like that
units.blurb: Every structural feature was built to render triangles. CUDA added scatter, pointers, a scratchpad, and permission to stop pretending.

units.title: The throughput machine
units.blurb: A GPU does not make any instruction stream fast. It makes stalling free.

units.title: The execution model
units.blurb: The warp is the unit of execution and the block is the unit of cooperation. Neither is the thread.

units.title: The memory hierarchy
units.blurb: DRAM latency is about 100x shared memory, and local memory is DRAM wearing a disguise.

units.title: Coalescing
units.blurb: A ratio, not a rule: maximise bytes used over bytes transferred. The compiler cannot see this and the profiler must.

units.title: Shared memory and banks
units.blurb: It decouples the access pattern you want from the one DRAM rewards, and has its own 32-way striping rule you must not violate instead.

units.title: The resource budget
units.blurb: Occupancy is a budget outcome, not a goal. You compute it; you do not chase it.

units.title: Latency hiding
units.blurb: Latency is hidden by having something else to issue, which is exactly why 100% occupancy is not the target.

units.title: Roofline and the three limiters
units.blurb: Memory, compute or latency. Speed of Light tells you which in two numbers, before you guess.

units.title: Strides and the dispatcher
units.blurb: A transpose is free because a stride is a lie you tell about memory. One aten call routes on device, layout, autograd and autocast.

units.title: Autograd
units.blurb: The tape is built during the forward pass. backward() is a topological traversal of a graph you did not know you were making.

units.title: Naive to tiled GEMM
units.blurb: The same five loops from the algorithms part, now as thread-block, warp and thread tiles.

units.title: CuTe layouts
units.blurb: Layout algebra turns index arithmetic back into algebra, and a swizzle into a composition.

units.title: The number formats
units.blurb: E4M3, E5M2, E2M1. Sixteen values, and the whole dynamic range is 3.58 binades.

units.title: Block scaling
units.blurb: Shrink the scale's scope until the outliers stop poisoning the block. Two levels, because the first one's format is narrow.

units.title: Rounding and Hadamard
units.blurb: Round-to-nearest stagnates at 0.5 where stochastic rounding reaches 101.0. Two orthogonal fixes for two different problems.

units.title: Transformer arithmetic
units.blurb: A config file is a complete performance model. Params, FLOPs, bytes and step time all follow from eight numbers.

units.title: Online softmax and FlashAttention
units.blurb: Reformulating a global reduction as a streaming one lets you compute an NxN matrix without ever storing it. It is exact.

units.title: Inference is two machines
units.blurb: Prefill is compute-bound and decode is memory-bound. Batch-1 decode wastes 99.66% of an H100 regardless of model size.

units.title: The parallelism taxonomy
units.blurb: Each dimension buys a specific memory saving with a specific collective. Map the worst collective to the fastest wire.

units.title: What actually breaks at scale
units.blurb: 466 interruptions in 54 days on 16,384 GPUs, and six of them were silent data corruption.

units.title: The chip with no operating system
units.blurb: Your main() is the system. There is no boot, no scheduler and no one to catch you.

units.title: The abstraction has a cost
units.blurb: digitalWrite and PORTB do the same thing, and one costs 26x more. The optimiser provably cannot fix it.

units.title: Time, interrupts and volatile
units.blurb: The compiler may delete code you need, because it cannot see the hardware or the interrupt. And volatile is not atomic.

units.title: Wider machines
units.blurb: The same C on a machine with enough registers produces different code and different problems.

units.title: Where determinism goes to die
units.blurb: An OS buys abstraction and sells determinism. Knowing which side you are on is the architectural decision.

units.title: Actuators and FOC
units.blurb: A PI controller cannot track a sinusoid with zero error. That sentence is why field-oriented control exists.

units.title: Control loops
units.blurb: PID properly, then cascade, and why the loop rates differ by four orders of magnitude.

units.title: Estimation
units.blurb: The Kalman filter is inverse-variance weighting. The off-diagonals are the punchline.

units.title: Kinematics
units.blurb: Gimbal lock is a Jacobian going to zero, and you can watch it happen to six significant figures.

units.title: Planning
units.blurb: Configuration space, sampling, and why a correct planner over a silently wrong domain is the bug you will actually write.

units.title: Physical intelligence
units.blurb: The System 1 / System 2 split in modern robot policies is cascade control, rediscovered.

units.title: The thermodynamic floor
units.blurb: Erasing a bit costs kT ln 2. A 3 nm gate sits four orders of magnitude above it, and a 1990s gate sat eight.

units.title: The walls we are hitting
units.blurb: Moving a 64-bit word 10 mm costs 82 pJ and the arithmetic on it costs a few. Measure work in bytes moved.

units.title: What else a computer could be
units.blurb: Quantum speedup is interference cancelling wrong answers, not trying everything at once. A 3-qubit circuit is an 8x8 matrix.
